name: Ireland
note: In Ireland the doctor who attended the deceased during the final illness gives a certificate of the cause of death to a relative, who must attend any registrar within three months to give the particulars (including the deceased's PPS number) and sign the register; reportable deaths (violent, unnatural, unexplained, or not from an illness treated within a month) must be reported to the coroner, who then supplies the particulars to the registrar. The register of deaths is a single national register kept by an tArd-Chláraitheoir (the General Register Office), and the PPS number on the entry lets public bodies that are 'specified bodies' share the death under the Social Welfare Consolidation Act 2005; electoral registration authorities may require death information from the GRO. Anyone may obtain a copy of the entry (without the PPS number). There is no official route for banks or other private bodies. An Act of 2024 providing for online registration within 28 days and direct notification of deaths by hospitals and doctors has not yet commenced.

steps.title: Death is verified by a doctor, nurse or paramedic
steps.who: A registered medical practitioner, or in practice a nurse or paramedic under professional guidance.
steps.summary: No statutory rule on verification (pronouncement) of death was found; recorded as unverified.

steps.title: Doctors, nurses and others must report a reportable death to the coroner
steps.who: Any doctor, nurse or midwife involved in the deceased's care or present at death, any doctor who examines the body, paramedics, the funeral undertaker, the person in charge of a mortuary or institution, the occupier of the dwelling, carers, custodians, and the registrar of deaths.
steps.trigger: A death that is violent, unnatural, by misadventure, unexpected or unexplained, possibly due to negligence, from a cause other than an illness treated by a doctor within one month, or listed in the Second Schedule.

deadline.text: as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the reportable death

steps.summary: Knowingly failing to report is an offence (class B fine). Where no medical certificate is procurable or it is unsatisfactory, the coroner may inquire into the death and hold an inquest.

steps.title: Gardaí report reportable deaths to the coroner
steps.who: A member of the Garda Síochána (to whom other persons may report the death).
steps.trigger: Becoming aware of a reportable death.
steps.summary: The Garda must report the death to the coroner for the district where the body is lying.

steps.title: Attending doctor gives the certificate of cause of death to the informant
steps.who: The registered medical practitioner who attended the deceased during the illness that preceded death.
steps.trigger: A death following an illness attended by a doctor, not referred to the coroner.
steps.summary: The informant takes the certificate to any registrar with the death registration form; there is no independent medical examiner review. (The 2024 Act would replace this with direct notification by the hospital or doctor to the GRO within five working days; not commenced.)

steps.title: Relative attends any registrar to register the death
steps.who: A relative, civil partner, cohabitant, next of kin, personal representative or religious superior with knowledge of the particulars; if none can be found or all are incapable, any other qualified informant (person present, occupier, chief officer of the hospital or institution, finder, person taking charge of or disposing of the body).

deadline.text: within 3 months from the date of the death

steps.summary: The informant gives the required particulars, including the deceased's PPS number, and signs the register in the registrar's presence. After three months a Superintendent Registrar may serve a notice requiring attendance.

steps.title: Coroner gives the registrar a certificate of the particulars
steps.who: The coroner who held or adjourned an inquest, ordered a post-mortem and decided not to hold an inquest, or inquired without either.
steps.trigger: Conclusion of the coroner's inquiry, inquest or post-mortem decision.
steps.summary: The registrar in the area where the body lay registers the death from the coroner's certificate as the Ard-Chláraitheoir directs.

steps.title: Coroner may authorise disposal of the body before registration
steps.who: The coroner, to a relative, the undertaker or another person in charge of the funeral.
steps.trigger: A death on which the coroner has held, or may hold, an inquest.
steps.summary: Burial or cremation in Ireland is not generally gated on registration; this is the statutory coroner authorisation recorded in the Act.

steps.title: Entry is made in the national register of deaths kept by an tArd-Chláraitheoir
steps.who: The registrar enters the death in the register maintained by an tArd-Chláraitheoir (General Register Office).
steps.summary: There is one national register of deaths, which may be held in non-paper form.

steps.title: Anyone may obtain a certified copy or extract of the death entry
steps.who: Any person who applies in writing and pays the fee, to an tArd-Chláraitheoir, a Superintendent Registrar, a registrar or an authorised officer.

steps.title: Registered death reaches the Department of Social Protection via the PPS number
steps.who: An tArd-Chláraitheoir (GRO) and the Department of Social Protection, both specified bodies for PPSN-based information sharing.
steps.trigger: Registration of the death with the deceased's PPS number.
steps.latencyNote: no time set (SWCA s. 265; CRA s. 66 read) (swca-2005-s265)
steps.summary: The death entry carries the PPS number and the Social Welfare Consolidation Act 2005 lets specified bodies share information keyed on it. That the Department is notified automatically on registration is the official position but could not be confirmed from a reachable official page.

steps.title: Revenue may obtain death information from other specified bodies
steps.who: The Revenue Commissioners, a specified body.
steps.trigger: A transaction with the person (or estate) for a relevant purpose.
steps.summary: PPSN-based sharing between specified bodies is available to the Revenue Commissioners; no statutory automatic death feed to Revenue was found.

steps.title: Electoral registration authority may require death information from the GRO
steps.who: Each registration authority (local authority) maintaining the register of electors.
steps.trigger: The authority's requirement, to keep the register accurate.
steps.summary: Since the Electoral Reform Act 2022 the GRO must furnish death information for the authority's area when required, and deceased persons are deleted from the register.

steps.title: Vital statistics on deaths
steps.who: The Minister, who may arrange for another Minister (in practice the Central Statistics Office) to compile and publish vital statistics.
steps.latencyNote: no time set; no regulations under s. 73(3) found (cra-2004-s73)
steps.summary: Information collected for vital statistics may not be disclosed in identifying form except for research or to HSE doctors with ministerial consent.

steps.title: Family tells banks, insurers and other private bodies
steps.who: The family or personal representative, usually presenting a death certificate.
steps.summary: No statute gives private bodies access to the register beyond the copies any person may obtain; the information-sharing gateways are limited to public specified bodies. Practice could not be confirmed from a reachable official page.

steps.title: Personal representatives may give notice to creditors
steps.summary: Notices to creditors (in practice newspaper advertisements) protect the personal representatives once the claims period expires.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Three months from the date of death (converted as 90 days). The Civil Registration (Electronic Registration) Act 2024 would shorten this to 28 days and allow online registration with a public services card, but those provisions had not commenced at the date of revision.

informantDuty.note: Relatives, civil partner, cohabitant, nominated next of kin, personal representative or religious superior first; other qualified informants only if none can be found or all are incapable.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No medical examiner system: the attending doctor's certificate goes via the informant to the registrar; only reportable deaths go to the coroner.

electronicRegistration.note: The informant must attend a registrar and sign the register; the electronic-registration provisions of the 2024 Act are not commenced.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register. There is a single national register of deaths kept by an tArd-Chláraitheoir, and the PPS number links public bodies, but no register that other bodies read death status from by law.

governmentPropagation.note: The death entry carries the PPS number and specified public bodies (including the GRO, government Ministers and Revenue) may share information keyed on it; electoral authorities may require death data from the GRO. Automatic notification of the Department of Social Protection is reported officially but not verified from a reachable page; passports and other bodies are not shown to be notified.

certificateAccess.note: Any person may apply for a certified copy, copy or extract; PPS numbers are omitted.

privateSectorVerification.note: No official route for private bodies beyond the copies any person may obtain. The GRO's statutory disclosure power (s. 66) names only public bodies and, as enacted, did not even list deaths.

gaps: gov.ie, www.gov.ie, www.citizensinformation.ie, www.welfare.ie, www.revenue.ie, www.hse.ie, www.dfa.ie (passports) and www.courts.ie were blocked by egress policy, so the operational death notification to the Department of Social Protection, Revenue, the HSE and the Passport Service could not be read from an official page. The DSP step and the governmentPropagation feature are unverified.

Civil Registration Act 2004 s. 66 (GRO disclosure to named public bodies) lists births, marriages and decrees but not deaths, both as enacted and as revised; the legal basis for death data reaching DSP is therefore taken to be PPSN sharing under Social Welfare Consolidation Act 2005 s. 265 and Sch. 5, which is an inference.

The Civil Registration (Electronic Registration) Act 2024 was partly commenced on 12 August 2024 (S.I. 435 of 2024, amending Sch. 1 particulars) but the substituted ss. 37, 41 and 42 (online registration within 28 days; hospital/doctor notification to the GRO within 5 working days) are shown as not commenced in the Law Reform Commission revision updated to 31 December 2025. Commencement after that date was not checked.
Civil Registration Act 2004 s. 37A (Covid-19 relief from attending in person) expired with the emergency period (last extended to 30 September 2021).
No statutory rule linking burial or cremation to registration was found (Cremation Regulations not searched); only the coroner's power to authorise disposal is recorded.
The Coroners Act 1962 Second Schedule (list of reportable deaths) was not transcribed.
Verification of the fact of death has no statutory basis found; the pronounce step is unverified.
